judged_text: The Zod uniqueness/validity schema (ZAddGuestsInputSchema) is defined inline inside the component per render, duplicating server-side validation with no shared schema module while the server defines its own ZAddGuestsInputSchema in addGuests.schema.ts. Two divergent definitions of 'valid guests' already exist: the client enforces uniqueness and non-empty via refine, the server enforces only per-item email format — the next change to one silently diverges from the other, and API consumers bypass the client checks entirely.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows two different validation schemas for the same API input. Client-side `AddGuestsDialog` defines `ZAddGuestsInputSchema` inline inside the component as `z.array(z.string().email()).refine(...)` enforcing uniqueness (and it’s recreated every render), while the server router uses `ZAddGuestsInputSchema` from `addGuests.schema.ts` as an object `{ bookingId: z.number(), guests: z.array(z.string().email()) }` with no uniqueness constraint. This is a real, diff-grounded maintainability/consistency issue: validation rules for “valid guests” can diverge, and non-UI callers can bypass the client-only uniqueness check.
